title: Tommaso Soderini, Milan, June-July 1477: five letters written in ordinary script whose words mostly do not read as Italian (possible word or letter substitution), unglossed
correspondents: Tommaso Soderini (signed "Tomaso So..."), Milan -> Lorenzo de' Medici
language: Italian? (disguised text in ordinary letters; uncertain)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza XLVIII, docs. 11-15
folio_note: Five leaves, rectos (versos addresses): each a full page in a fluent hand; some words read ("O magnifico ...", "madonna", "aveva", "conforteranno", "tutti loro"), but many do not ("ezamonte", "zogo"), and scattered words are heavily inked; the date lines are clear. Doc. 11 seen at 1272 px; 12-15 at 800 px.
status: Unsure whether this is cipher at all (a jargon or letter-substitution disguise, or only a hard hand); no gloss and no clear copy seen beside it.
why: If it is a disguise, it is a 1477 Milan correspondence of Lorenzo's ambassador, before the Pazzi war; the same writer's August 1481 letter (row below) is in true sign cipher.
verify: Transcribe doc. 11 at full size and test for word substitution (cover names) versus a letter cipher in Latin letters.

vetting_note: edition partly answers but does not settle cipher versus hard hand. Lettere II (1474-1478, ed. Fubini, 1hpdAAAAMAAJ, opened in Chrome): p. 432 cites 'T. Soderini a Lorenzo, 17 novembre, MAP, XLVIII, 13' and paraphrases it as ordinary content (the Sienese accepting an orator, Nov 1477), with no mention of cipher; 'XLVIII, 11', '12', '14', '15' probes hit only index pages and unrelated notes (pp. 96, 409, 412, 417, 529-560); 'Soderini' 20 pages, 'cifra' 9 pages (75, 180, 276 ...), 'gergo' 0. The editor's date (17 Nov) conflicts with the lead's 'luglio 1477' for doc. 13, so the identification needs checking. Leans not cipher (editor read doc. 13 as prose; n18 found ordinary Italian vowel patterns, no signs), but a not_cipher verdict needs a line-by-line reading of docs 11-15 at full size.
prior_unvetted: cipher or hard hand not settled at full size, and the edition not opened. Doc. 11 (A0000023, 1272 px) and 12-15 at server maximum: a fast, idiosyncratic hand in which many words read ('domani', 'madona', 'conforteranno', 'al campo', 'cavalli', 'gesto/gelo' for questo/quello, the date 'in Milano a di 8 luglio 1477' and the signature 'Tomaso Soderini' clear) and many do not, with vowel patterns and endings of ordinary Italian; no signs, figures or gloss. To decide: transcribe doc. 11 line by line and test whether the non-reading words follow a fixed letter swap, and search Lorenzo's Lettere II (1474-1478, ed. Fubini, Google Books 1hpdAAAAMAAJ, old interface in Chrome) for 'XLVIII, 11' ... 'XLVIII, 15' and 'Soderini luglio 1477': its notes and Rochon, La jeunesse de Laurent (1963), which uses Soderini's 1477 letters in MAP XLVIII without mention of cipher, would show whether the text was read as ordinary prose. The Google Books feed found no 'MAP, XLVIII, 11'-'15' citation.

date: c. 1488-89 (minute; signed on c. 509 bis "Lorenzo de Medici")
title: Lorenzo de' Medici to Giovanni Lanfredini, orator in Rome, c. 1488-89: autograph minute with about fourteen sign-cipher runs between clear words, bare
correspondents: Lorenzo de' Medici -> Giovanni Lanfredini, Florentine orator in Rome
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza CXXXVII, doc. 504 (cc. 509-510 bis)
folio_note: c. 509r: a dense clear minute (N.S. = the pope, Virginio Orsini?) with about 8 cipher runs of 10-40 signs (÷, π, +, 2, 3, 4, Latin-letter forms) in the middle and lower half; c. 509v: about 6 more runs; c. 509 bis r: signature; c. 510 bis v: address to Lanfredini.
status: Bare (1272 px on c. 509r, 800 px on the rest): no gloss; the cipher was written into the minute by Lorenzo's chancery.
why: An outgoing cipher letter of Lorenzo il Magnifico to his key ambassador in Rome in the years of the Innocent VIII alliance; Lanfredini's incoming cipher letters (and the Laurentian key sheets) are the obvious route to the key.
verify: Transcribe the runs; test the LXXII 178-188 and CXIX 115-127 keys (none is labelled Lanfredini); look for Lanfredini's own glossed letters of 1487-89 in MAP (e.g. filze L-LX).

The volume(s) covering Aug 1488 - Feb 1489 (Lettere XIII/XIV, after vol. XII febbraio-luglio 1488, OSJdAAAAMAAJ) have no Google Books record in the gdata feed (queries 'agosto 1488', 'ottobre 1488', 'febbraio 1489', 'Lettere 13/14'); the Books API quota is exhausted. Needed: Lettere XIII or XIV in a library, search 'CXXXVII, 504', 'Oddi', 'Baglioni'.
prior_unvetted: the printed Lettere not opened. The minute is a registered letter of Lorenzo to Giovanni Lanfredini: the Protocolli (Del Piazzo 1956) list it at 'M. a P., CXXXVII, 504' just before the letter of 27 Apr 1489, the Censimento (1964) places 'MAP, CXXXVII, 504' among the Lanfredini letters of November 1488, and Lettere XV (marzo-agosto 1489, ed. Boninger, Google Books oSQsAQAAMAAJ / JgcwAQAAMAAJ) cites it in its notes to the letter to Lanfredini of 28 Mar 1489 ('il testo di due suppliche riguardanti la costruzione e dotazione del convento fiorentino di San Gallo (MAP, CXXXVII, 504; cfr. Kent, Lorenzo de' Medici, pp. 97-99)'). Its text (answering Lanfredini's letters of the 11th and 13th on Perugia, the Baglioni and the Oddi, 'N.S.') belongs in Lettere XIV or XV, whose editors print Lorenzo's cipher passages from deciphered or register copies where they survive. Needed: Chrome search inside the Lettere volume for Oct 1488 - Feb 1489 and vol. XV for 'CXXXVII, 504' and 'Oddi', to see whether the letter is printed and whether its ~14 cipher runs are given in clear. The Lanfredini Naples edition (Corrispondenza degli ambasciatori fiorentini a Napoli, 1484-1487) ends before this letter. Every
